title: Quarantine partial-streams on disconnect with delayed-ACK backoff and GC
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When clients disconnect during a long-running streaming generation (tool calls or structured outputs), partial generations are left in the runtime and KV cache. These partials consume memory, can cause duplicate tool invocations if resumed incorrectly, and distort cost/latency metrics. Older clients sometimes do not send explicit resume tokens or ACKs, so we need a robust server-side quarantine+GC scheme that is backward-compatible and supports graceful resume for modern SDKs.

Goals:
- Ensure resources tied to disconnected streams are reclaimed in a bounded timeframe without losing the ability to resume for clients that support resume tokens.
- Prevent duplicate side effects (tool/function calls) on resume or retry.
- Provide observability (counts of quarantined partials, GC rate, resume success rate) and safety controls for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers.

Proposed approach:
1) Quarantine state: On unclean client disconnect (socket close, heartbeat timeout), mark the generation as QUARANTINED rather than immediately deleting. Store minimal resume metadata: model_id, sequence_offsets, causal_prefix_hash, resume_token, pending_tool_calls (ids + at-most-once markers), and TTL. Quarantined entries are read-only (no new appends).
2) Delayed-ACK backoff window: For clients that supported streaming ACKs (new SDKs), allow an exponential backoff window (initial 30s -> 2m -> 8m) during which runtime will accept a resume request and merge new tokens carefully. For legacy clients without ACKs, use a shorter default TTL (2m).
3) At-most-once tool semantics: Record the tool call id and response in the quarantined metadata. On resume, the runtime will detect previously executed tool calls and return cached responses instead of re-invoking. For side effects that cannot be cached, mark resume as non-idempotent and surface a resume failure to client; fallback policies (canary to cheaper model or restart generation) will be applied.
4) Quarantine GC: Background garbage collector with two tiers: soft-GC (reclaim ephemeral memory but keep resume tokens) after TTL1, hard-GC (delete metadata, free KV entries) after TTL2. TTLs configurable per deployment and overridable per-customer via console.
5) Compatibility layer: Introduce a server-side compatibility flag stream_resume_compat that provides heuristic resume for legacy clients (matching by session-cookie + generation fingerprint). This is opt-in for Dedicated/Private by default to avoid accidental duplicate side-effects for high-risk customers.
6) Observability & error codes: Add streaming metrics (quarantined_count, resume_success_rate, duplicate_tool_detected, gc_rate) and new API error codes: 409.RESUME_STALE, 410.RESUME_NOT_SUPPORTED, 425.GENERATION_QUARANTINED.

Edge cases and considerations:
- Partial structured outputs: If client requested structured output (JSON schema) and we only have partial parse tree, keep partial AST in quarantine and allow resume to reconcile. If schema validation failed on resume, surface structured-output regression alert.
- Tool/function calling during quarantine: If tool call was invoked but external RPC not confirmed, treat as potentially non-idempotent; default to marking resume as unsafe and require client to restart generation.
- Cost accounting: Bill only completed tokens; quarantined partials should report ephemeral accounting. Console will show quarantined token counts separately so customers can investigate.

Implementation plan, code areas:
- runtime/service/session_manager.go: add Quarantine metadata and state transitions.
- runtime/kv/compactor: GC two-tier pass and TTL configs.
- api/streaming.proto: add resume token semantics and new error codes (compat shim for older clients).
- sdk-js/sdk-go: add resume and ack semantics; opt-in compatibility toggle.
- console: UI for quarantined streams and per-customer TTL override.

Rollout strategy:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag quarantine-streams = true.
- Phase 1 (canary): enable for 10% of host-api traffic, no compatibility heuristics. Monitor metrics for duplicate tool calls and resume_success_rate for 48h.
- Phase 2: enable compatibility heuristics in Dedicated staging accounts only; run extended tests with enterprise partners.
- Phase 3: enable for all hosted customers with conservative defaults, surface console toggle for enterprise.

Why this is different from existing tickets:
Most existing streaming tickets focus on backpressure bookkeeping and stream eviction heuristics. This ticket combines quarantine semantics, delayed-ACK backoff, and explicit at-most-once tooling semantics to address tool-calling edge cases and structured-output resumption. It includes a GC strategy and compatibility opt-in for legacy clients.
acceptance_criteria: On unclean disconnect, generation state transitions to QUARANTINED and is queryable via admin API.
Resume succeeds for new SDK clients within backoff window and returns identical completed tokens and cached tool responses.
Attempting to resume a quarantined non-idempotent generation returns 409.RESUME_STALE or 410.RESUME_NOT_SUPPORTED as appropriate.
Soft-GC triggers after TTL1 and reduces memory usage without removing resume tokens; hard-GC runs after TTL2 and frees KV entries.
Console surfaces quarantined stream metrics and allows per-customer TTL override for Dedicated/Private deployments.
No increase in duplicate tool invocations after canary rollout (<=0.1% relative increase), verified by related_prs smoke tests and production traces.
steps: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and SDK leads (link in docs_links).
Implement Quarantine state machine and API error codes in runtime/service (feature-flagged).
Add KV metadata layout and GC pass; expose TTL config in console.
SDK changes: add resume(), ack heartbeats, and opt-in compatibility toggle.
Integration tests: resume happy path, duplicate-tool detection, structured-output reconciliation, GC behavior.
Canary rollout to 10% hosted traffic; collect metrics for 72h.
Gradual rollout to Dedicated with console toggles and customer communications.
risks: If compatibility heuristics are too permissive, we may re-trigger side-effects (tool calls) leading to customer-impacting duplicates.
Incorrect TTL defaults could either leak memory (too long) or break legitimate resume flows (too short).
Complexity of structured-output partial-asts increases surface area for resume bugs and validation regressions.
Observability gaps might make it hard to triage stale quarantined entries without new dashboarding.
success_metrics: resume_success_rate >= 98% for new SDKs within backoff window
mean quarantined memory per-host reduced by 60% after soft-GC
quarantined_count metric trends to zero for normal traffic patterns (no persistent leaks)
